lines: A 3HP blank panel that you load SVG images onto from its own right-click menu, over a choice of six background finishes
Note — the panel shows only its background until you load a picture: right-click it and choose Load SVG...
Note — in Single mode one picture is drawn centred on the panel; in Multiple mode each picture you load is dropped at a random place and angle, tilted by up to 18 degrees either way.
Note — the mode cannot be changed while any picture is loaded. The menu shows a greyed line saying to delete the loaded SVGs first.
Note — each loaded picture gets its own submenu carrying Lock, which holds it in place when Shake runs, and Delete, which removes it whether it is locked or not.
Note — the first time the plugin loads it makes a Sticksy folder in your Rack user folder, with Stickers and Animation inside it, and copies the bundled artwork there.
Note — the file browser opens in that Stickers folder the first time you load a picture in a session.
Note — an SVG that cannot be read is replaced by the plugin's own fallback picture, so a broken path shows something rather than nothing.
Note — the background starts on Black, and every loaded picture, its position and its lock state are saved with the patch.
Menu — Mode: Single, Multiple — chooses whether one picture is drawn centred or several are scattered at random places and angles
Menu — Load SVG... — opens a file browser and puts the SVG you pick onto the panel
Menu — Shake — throws every unlocked picture to a new random place and angle; it appears only in Multiple mode
Menu — Storage: Referenced, Save in Sticksy Library — chooses whether the patch points at the file where you found it or at a copy the module makes in the Sticksy folder of your Rack user folder
Menu — Lock — on the submenu for one loaded picture: holds that picture where it is when Shake runs
Menu — Delete — on the submenu for one loaded picture: removes that picture, locked or not
Menu — Background: Neutral, Wood, Metal, Paper, Black, White — sets the finish of the panel the pictures are drawn on
SticksyBlank3.notes: This model has no parameters, inputs or outputs: config(0,0,0,0) at src/plugin.cpp:188, and the four blank models differ only in the HP passed to the shared SticksyBlankModule constructor (src/plugin.cpp:341 to 344). Everything the module does is on the panel context menu, built at src/plugin.cpp:319. setMode at src/plugin.cpp:204 returns without doing anything while any sticker is loaded. The Background menu is cosmetic, which STYLE would normally leave out, but a decorative blank panel is the exception it names: the finish is what the module is for. init() at src/plugin.cpp:836 calls ensureDefaultSticksyLibraryInstalled, which creates <Rack user folder>/Sticksy/Stickers and <Rack user folder>/Sticksy/Animation/vc_cat and copies the plugin's bundled SVGs into them; it writes nothing else and keeps no settings file. Storage is the plugin-wide menu item that changes behaviour rather than appearance, so by STYLE's rule it is written on all four blanks. Multiple-mode placement is random within one HP of each panel edge, with a rotation of plus or minus 18 degrees (src/plugin.cpp:283).

lines: A 12HP panel that steps through a numbered sequence of SVG files, one frame per clock pulse, with an end-of-cycle output
Each rising edge past 1V moves to the next frame, in whichever order the play mode sets
A rising edge past 1V returns the sequence to its first frame and points ping pong forward again; a reset and a clock arriving in the same sample are settled in the reset's favour
A 1ms 10V pulse each time the sequence finishes a pass through the frames, or on every clock pulse while a single frame is loaded
Note — the panel is empty until you load a sequence: right-click it and choose Load Flipbook Image..., then pick any file of a numbered set such as cat_01.svg.
Note — picking one file loads every SVG in the same folder whose name matches it apart from the number on the end, ordered by that number, to a limit of 128 frames.
Note — a file whose name does not end in a number is loaded on its own, as a sequence of one frame.
Note — with nothing patched into the clock input nothing advances and the panel holds the frame it is on.
Note — a file that cannot be read is replaced by the plugin's own fallback picture, so a missing frame shows something rather than a gap.
Note — the first time the plugin loads it makes a Sticksy folder in your Rack user folder and copies the bundled artwork there, including a sixteen-frame cat sequence.
Note — the file browser opens in that Animation folder the first time you load a flipbook in a session.
Note — in Random mode the end-of-cycle output fires once every time as many clock pulses have arrived as there are frames, rather than at any particular frame.
Menu — Load Flipbook Image... — opens a file browser and loads the numbered sequence that the file you pick belongs to
Menu — Load Background Image... — loads one SVG that is drawn behind every frame
Menu — Clear Background — removes the background picture; it is greyed out while there is none
Menu — Play Mode: Forward, Reverse, Ping Pong, Random — sets the order the clock steps through the frames

0.why: src/plugin.cpp:535 passes the voltage to a dsp::SchmittTrigger, whose default thresholds are 0V and 1V, and reads it with getVoltage() and no channel index

1.why: src/plugin.cpp:531 passes the voltage to a dsp::SchmittTrigger, whose default thresholds are 0V and 1V, and reads it with getVoltage() and no channel index

0.why: src/plugin.cpp:582 writes 10 or 0 with no channel index from a dsp::PulseGenerator triggered for 1e-3 seconds at line 581

SticksyFlipbook.notes: The three jacks carry no lettering on the panel; res/panels/flipbook/flipbook_12hp.svg is plain artwork, and the only names are the configInput and configOutput strings CLK, RST and EOC (src/plugin.cpp:385 to 387). The reset is tested before the clock and sets a flag that skips the clock in the same sample (src/plugin.cpp:531 to 536). MAX_FRAMES is 128 (src/plugin.cpp:362). A reset when no frames are loaded does nothing at all, because resetPlaybackToFirstFrame returns early on an empty sequence. This model has no parameters. Unlike the four blanks it carries no Storage menu item: a flipbook always references the files where they were found.
